Hi Maya — great meeting yesterday. As promised, attaching a concise summary of a tiered commit structure we think maps well to ClearSight’s usage profile (bursty inference, heavy short-sequence chat). Key points up front:

- Proposal: 3-tier committed pool (Pilot, Production, Burst) with escalating unit discounts tied to committed token volumes and a small monthly reserved baseline. Pilot = 250k tokens/mo commit for 3 months (intro credits + 15% off hosted per-token). Production = 2M tokens/mo commit (25% off + dedicated routing options). Burst add-on available for seasonal spikes.
- Optimizations: recommend enabling prefix KV caching for chat sessions and an aggressive batching profile for background embedding jobs. Together we project 20–30% unit cost reduction at pilot scale, increasing to ~45% at production with quantization enabled.
- Quantization: recommend per-model A/B validation starting with 8-bit asymmetric quant (Q8) on non-critical models; hold LLMQ8 for high-precision prompts until we validate output drift with your eval set. Karthik (cc) will provide the validation checklist.

Attached: 20270625_optimize_tiered_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing summary + sample rollout timeline).

Next steps: 1) Confirm pilot commit and dates, 2) Schedule a 60-minute technical workshop (Karthik + infra) to validate latency/accuracy tradeoffs, 3) Procurement loop-in for SOW and PO.

Thanks — Jonas

Hi all — couple of technical notes ahead of the workshop to set expectations: 

- Q8 behavior: on our internal benchmarks Q8 reduces token-cost by ~38% vs FP16 for GPT-like decoder models with negligible latency delta. However, quantization can shift probability mass slightly on edge-case prompts (rare tokenization artifacts). For ClearSight’s tolerance we should: (a) pick a 5k–10k validation suite drawn from your customer interactions, (b) run constrained RMSE and top-k token divergence metrics, and (c) validate downstream NER/fraud tasks before any production rollout.

- Caching strategy: prefix KV caching yields the best bang-for-buck when session lengths >3 turns and when there is a high degree of token overlap across requests. I recommend enabling prefix caching with a TTL of 30 minutes for chat sessions and a separate cache for system prompts. We’ll provide cache hit-rate dashboards.

- Fallbacks: implement automatic model fallback routing: if quantized model returns a confidence score below threshold or latency spikes >500ms, route to FP16 instance for that request. Redwood Runtime supports per-request policy overrides.

I’ll bring a short runbook to the workshop that outlines the exact eval commands and metrics. Looking forward to the session.

—Karthik
